title: The Infiltrator Deep Dive
youtubeTitle: Subspace Lattice Academy Ep.10 — Infiltrators: Warp & Target Lock
description: Phase Runners with folding-drives: how an Infiltrator warps through unclaimed space, and how hostile coverage Target Locks the engines and kills the warp. Real Heuristic AI play (seed 12100).

scenes.headline: The Infiltrator Deep Dive
scenes.subhead: Warp through unclaimed space — until the net locks your engines.
scenes.voiceover: Episode ten: the Infiltrator. Episode seven told you to save warps for real targets. Episode eight covered the Heavy wing. Now the Phase Runner gets its mechanical moment — generated from real Heuristic AI play.

scenes.headline: Phase Runners
bullets: Folding-drive jumps while you are undetected
Target Lock → one orthogonal crawl — no warp
scenes.voiceover: Fiction calls them Phase Runners: folding-drives that jump through space your Sensor Net does not yet claim. The engine rule is simpler. While an Infiltrator is not Target Locked, it may warp to a legal destination. The moment hostile coverage detects it, the engines lock — one orthogonal step only.

scenes.moveLabel: Ply 1 — White warps across the sector
scenes.voiceover: Ply one of a Heuristic versus Heuristic match. White’s Infiltrator leaves three-zero and lands at nine-ten — a ten-cell warp through space neither net fully owned. That is the fold looking like aggression. Respect it; do not copy it blindly.

scenes.moveLabel: Ply 6 — Black answers with a warp
scenes.voiceover: Ply six. Black mirrors the idea: nine-ten to nine-zero. Long warps early are tempo weapons when the destination is safe. The lesson is not “always teleport” — it is “warp only when the landing square is not a gift.”

scenes.caption: Warps hunting Heavy material
scenes.voiceover: Midgame. The AI starts spending warps on real targets — Heavy pieces sitting where an Infiltrator can fold in and capture.

scenes.moveLabel: Ply 18 — warp capture on a Beam
scenes.voiceover: Ply eighteen. Black’s Infiltrator warps from nine-zero to four-five and removes White’s Beam. That is the “real target” Episode seven promised — material, not a panic hop into blue glow.

Two plies later the same runner folds again and takes White’s other heavy. Warp plus capture is why you keep Infiltrators alive through the opening — they are strike craft, not Escorts with a gimmick.

scenes.headline: Target Lock kills the fold
bullets: Detected in enemy Sovereign Space → Target Locked
Locked pieces crawl one orthogonal step
No Chebyshev jump while the engines are seized
scenes.voiceover: Now the other half of the lesson. Push an Infiltrator into hostile coverage and Target Lock seizes the engines. The piece still exists — but the warp is gone until it exits the lock. Immobile aggression is just a gift.
Ply forty-five. Black’s Infiltrator sits at six-five — already Target Locked inside White’s net. The folding-drive is dead on this square. Watch what the AI is forced to do next.

scenes.prompt: The Infiltrator is Target Locked. Can it warp to safety — or only crawl?
scenes.voiceover: Pause and predict. Locked engines. Is a five-cell escape legal, or only a single orthogonal step?
scenes.revealVoiceover: Ply forty-six: one step — six-five to six-four — capturing an Escort on the crawl. That is all a locked Phase Runner can do. Hostile coverage did not destroy the ship; it killed the warp.

scenes.headline: Warp smart — fear the lock
scenes.voiceover: Infiltrators: warp through unclaimed space for real targets, and never forget that Target Lock turns a Phase Runner into a foot soldier. Next: the third win condition — Lockout — when immobility is defeat.
